sentences: I check the departure board at the station and note that the 07:42 to Crewe is running on time.
I measure the distance between the rails with a gauge and record the reading in my notebook.
I walk along the platform to the far end and stand behind the yellow line as the train approaches.
I sit in the window seat and watch the overhead wires pass above the train through the glass.
I pull the emergency door release handle only when the train has stopped and the conductor gives permission.
I count the number of carriages on the freight train as it passes the level crossing.
I check the timetable on my phone and see that the next service to Leeds departs in twelve minutes.
I place my suitcase on the luggage rack above the seat and return to my place.
I insert my ticket into the barrier at the gate and walk through when the flaps open.
I listen to the automated announcement that tells passengers to mind the gap between the train and the platform.
I watch the signal change from red to green and hear the train's horn sound once before it moves.
I walk through the vestibule to the next carriage and find an empty seat near the door.
I check the reservation label above the seat to confirm that it matches the number on my ticket.
I stand on the footbridge and count the trains that pass beneath on the four tracks below.
I note the locomotive number on the front of the train and write it on the back of my notebook.
I open the window in the door and hold my hand in the air that moves past as the train travels.
I read the safety instructions card in the seat pocket and check the location of the nearest exit.
I watch the maintenance workers inspect the track with a machine that measures the alignment of the rails.
I wait on the platform until the train stops and the doors slide open with a chime.
I check the clock above the ticket office and calculate that the train is four minutes late.
